ladder.verdict: FAILED at CP6. 8 walls ON TIME (steps 0.680 / 1.284 / 1.812 / 2.794 / 3.926 / 4.606 / 4.983 / 5.512B = 1.00-1.89x run 5); CP6 not cleared by its deadline 12.232B steps: the deciding eval 12,231,114,752 reached 82.28% (CP5; the greedy stops ~5.6k u before the CP6 curtain). Stopped at ~12.42B steps. In total ticks CP6 was still PENDING (15.18B of a 16.44B deadline), but slot 3 is judged in steps.

summary: Slot 3 kept run 5's two threads and made the tree TEACH: labels from every MCTS tree as an extra loss next to PPO's (--tree-labels 0.1, commit 2a4f8edd) - policy target = the children that beat the policy's own greedy child (sibling-rank weights), value target = the node's percentile rank in its tree on a separate head (PPO's critic untouched). Run azr1b3_tl1 (run 5 + labels, from step 0, RTX 5080 ~250k steps/s): 8 walls ON TIME at 1.00-1.89x run 5 in steps (0.93-1.82x in total ticks), then FAILED CP6 (deadline 12.23B steps) at 82.3%, best eval 82.31%. After CP5 every rise came from a search line learned through the curriculum ~0.5B steps later (64.9 -> 69.7 -> 72.3 -> 82.2%); the labels were active (2-19% of nodes informative, ~11% of a label batch) but never moved the greedy by themselves, and 6 of 8 walls came >30% slower than run 5 (one seed each). For the user's question: teaching the policy from the tree's sibling ranks did not replace or speed up the line -> spawn path; what the tree should teach is still open. Run 2 azr1b3_tl2 (slot 1's finishing recipe + the labels, paired with azr1b1_pool1) was stopped by ROUND OVER at 0.56B steps (first ramp pending; 6.1% at 529M vs slot 1's 1.8% - one early mark, not a wall). Next: finish tl2 against slot 1, and if labels stay, teach per decision only where the tree's margin is large.
